blocks.text: Mastering Zoom for virtual event hosts on Mac

Managing a virtual event on a Mac demands precision. You need to switch between slides, admit attendees, and monitor the chat. Using the mouse for every action wastes precious seconds. Learn the keyboard shortcuts to keep your focus on the participants.

items: Use ⌘ ⇧ A to toggle your audio quickly.
Use ⌘ ⇧ V to toggle your video feed.
Use ⌘ ⇧ S to start or stop screen sharing.
Use ⌘ ⇧ H to show or hide the meeting controls.
Use ⌘ ⇧ W to switch to Gallery View during a presentation.

blocks.text: Common mistakes when hosting on Mac

Many hosts struggle with permission settings. macOS requires specific access for screen recording and camera usage. If your screen share shows a black box, check System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording. Ensure Zoom is enabled there. This is a frequent issue after a macOS update.
If you are unsure where a setting is, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to find it. Lazur will draw a circle around the specific menu item for you.

blocks.text: Why virtual event hosts choose Mac

Apple Silicon Macs offer great performance for streaming. You can run Zoom alongside other apps without major slowdowns. Keep your system updated to the latest version of macOS. This prevents compatibility issues with Zoom Workplace features.
Using Lazur to manage your event workflow

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It helps you manage your day between meetings. You can ask it to set reminders for speaker briefings or draft follow-up emails. It does not click buttons for you, but it guides you through the interface.
Pro tips for Zoom meeting management

items: Hardwire your internet connection if possible.
Close unnecessary background apps to save memory.
Use a dedicated external microphone for better audio quality.
Test your virtual background before the event starts.
Keep your run of show document open in a separate window.

blocks.text: Managing an event is stressful. Automation helps reduce the admin burden. Use your calendar to block out time for deep work. If you find yourself repeating the same tasks, create templates. This saves time and keeps your process consistent.
Handling attendee questions during the event

During live events, the chat can move fast. Keep the chat window detached. You can drag it to a second monitor if you have one. This allows you to monitor questions while keeping your presentation visible. If you miss a question, don't panic. Acknowledge it later during a Q&A session.
Staying organized as a virtual host

Keep a physical notebook or a digital app for quick notes. When a speaker mentions a change, write it down immediately. Do not rely on memory alone. Use the last five minutes of every hour to review your schedule. This keeps you ahead of the next session.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me in Zoom?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Zoom for you. It guides you, points at items, and answers questions while you do the work.

faq.question: How do I fix a black screen share on Mac?
faq.answer: Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and ensure Zoom has permission to record your screen.

faq.question: Is Lazur compatible with all Mac models?
faq.answer: Lazur works on all Macs running macOS, including Apple Silicon and Intel-based models.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to dictate notes during a meeting?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold the fn key to dictate text directly into any app, including your notes or meeting documents.
